body: For a frequency band defined by lower and upper bounds [f_low, f_high) and a spectral decomposition with N frequency bins indexed i=1..N, each with a complex amplitude A_i and frequency f_i where f_low <= f_i < f_high: the distribution is the ordered vector v = (|A_1|^2, |A_2|^2, ..., |A_N|^2), where |A_i|^2 is the energy of bin i. The parameters are the band bounds and the spectral decomposition method. The persistence mechanism is the explicit storage of the N-tuple of non-negative scalars ordered by bin index. [formal: the mathematical representation | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Cepstral sequence is an ordered array of cepstral coefficients indexed by coefficient position, representing signal characteristics in the cepstral domain. Parameters: (1) number of coefficients N (typically 12-20 for speech), (2) coefficient type — filterbank-based MFCC, DFT-based, or DCT-based cepstral coefficients, (3) normalization method — mean-normalized, variance-normalized, or raw. The persistence mechanism maps (coefficient type, count, normalization) to a fixed-length vector c[1..N] where each element c[i] represents the i-th cepstral coefficient. [formal: cepstrum | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A Kaiser window is a parameterized family of window functions defined by the zeroth-order modified Bessel function. Its formula is: w(n) = I₀(πβ√(1−((2n−(N−1))/(N))²)) / I₀(πβ) for 0 ≤ n ≤ N−1, where I₀ is the zeroth-order modified Bessel function of the first kind, N is the window length, and β is the shape parameter. The β parameter controls the tradeoff between main-lobe width and side-lobe attenuation: β = 0 yields a rectangular window; β = 2.43 is optimal for DFT analysis; β = 3.44 approximates a Hamming window; β = 5 gives ≈−43 dB side lobes; β = 6 gives ≈−47 dB; β ≥ 9 approaches the Blackman-Harris form. The family is designed to achieve the maximum main-lobe concentration for a given side-lobe level — optimal for a specified side-lobe constraint. Persistence mechanism: the Bessel-function formula codified in DSP literature and implemented in all major signal-processing toolkits. [formal: fenestra kaißer | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.5]

For a frequency band with N energy bins having energies E_1, E_2, ..., E_N: the RMS energy is the square root of the mean of squared energies. The parameter is the frequency band definition (lower and upper bounds). The persistence mechanism is RMS = sqrt((1/N) * sum(E_i^2)) over N bins within the band. Display trailer: [formal: rms energy | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Spectral-onset detects the emergence of new frequency content by measuring the increase in spectral energy between consecutive time frames. Given consecutive power spectra P[k,t] and P[k,t-1], the spectral onset function O[t] = max(P[k,t] - P[k,t-1], 0) summed across frequency bins. Parameters: (1) the power spectrum P[k,t] as the input domain, (2) the frame rate and windowing scheme, (3) the frequency band of interest. The persistence mechanism is the frame-to-frame difference of the power spectrum, thresholded by a half-wave rectifier, which distinguishes onset frames from sustained or decaying content. [formal: spectralis initium | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Spectral-subband partitions the frequency axis into a contiguous range [f_lower, f_upper] within the overall spectrum. Given a sampling rate F_s and N frequency bins indexed by k = 0..N-1, a subband is defined by index range [k_1, k_2] where f_lower = k_1·F_s/N and f_upper = (k_2+1)·F_s/N. Parameters: (1) the spectral resolution (bin width F_s/N), (2) the frequency range [f_lower, f_upper] defining the subband, (3) the spectral representation (power spectrum, magnitude spectrum, or coefficients) over which the subband operates. The persistence mechanism is the contiguous index range [k_1, k_2] over the frequency axis, which enables independent processing of frequency content within the band. [formal: spectralis subbanda | substrate: matter | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Text-linguistics is a human-made discipline of linguistics — the study of the structure, coherence, and function of extended texts (discourses) as structured wholes that extend beyond the sentence level. Two parameters carve the construct: (1) the unit of analysis is the text or discourse as an integrated semantic-pragmatic entity, governed by relations of cohesion (grammatical and lexical ties across clauses), coherence (understandable logical and semantic connections), and communicative purpose (the function the text serves in interaction); (2) the analytical tools include discourse structure analysis (narrative, argumentative, expository patterns), information structure (theme-rheme, given-new), referential continuity (pronoun chains, anaphora resolution), and textual genre conventions that organize texts for specific communicative situations. Text-linguistics persists as a discipline that produces descriptions of textual organization across languages, models of discourse interpretation, and applications in text technology, rhetoric, discourse analysis, and language pedagogy. Paradigmatic cases: Halliday and Hasan's cohesion analysis, van Dijk's discourse semantics, rhetorical structure theory. [formal: textus-linguistica | substrate: mind | horizon: decades | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

The vocal-tract model is a human-made model of the vocal tract as an acoustic filter cavity in speech production, describing how the shape of the vocal tract resonates to shape the glottal source into speech sounds. Parameters: area function along tract length, formant frequencies and bandwidths, articulatory positions. Persistence mechanism: the model is formalized as acoustic tube theory, implemented in speech synthesis and analysis software, and taught in phonetics; it persists as a reusable filter component of the source-filter framework. [formal: vocal-tract | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.07]

The attack-time is a non-negative real-valued duration representing the time elapsed from the onset of a sound to the peak of its amplitude envelope. Parameters: (1) the amplitude envelope function of the sound, (2) the detected onset point (zero-crossing of the envelope derivative), (3) the peak point (global maximum of the envelope within the attack phase). The persistence mechanism identifies the onset as the first zero-crossing of the envelope's first derivative after silence, and the peak as the local maximum of the envelope following that onset, then computes the time difference. [formal: attack-time | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.03]

Spectral increase is a metric capturing the temporal rise of spectral energy between consecutive analysis frames. Computed as the difference between the current frame's total spectral energy and the preceding frame's energy, normalized by the preceding frame's energy. Positive values indicate energy growth; negative values indicate decay. [formal: augmentatio spectralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

spectral-band-peak(f_low, f_high) = max{E[i]} for all bins i where f_low <= f_center[i] < f_high. Parameters: f_low (Hz, lower band boundary), f_high (Hz, upper band boundary), sampling_rate (Hz, determines bin center frequencies), n_fft (int, FFT window size). Persistence: pointwise maximum of the power spectral density within the band. [formal: spectral-band-peak | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The spectral-power-distribution is a non-negative real-valued function over a discrete frequency domain representing how signal power is distributed across frequency bins. Parameters: (1) the input signal, (2) the number of frequency bins N, (3) the sampling rate or frequency resolution. Computation: take the magnitude spectrum |X[k]| of the input signal, compute P[k] = |X[k]|² / N for each bin k, yielding a discrete distribution over frequencies. The values P[k] are non-negative and sum to the total signal power, forming a power distribution across the frequency axis. [formal: CONCEPT | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Spectral-band-variance is a spectral analysis parameter quantifying the dispersion of spectral energy within a defined frequency sub-band of a spectrum at a given analysis frame. It is the band-localized (second-moment) statistic of the spectral-band moment family, computed from the per-bin energy values inside the band. Parameters: (1) the band's lower and upper frequency bounds (f_low, f_high, e.g. ISO 266 third-octave band edges or analyst-specified limits), (2) the per-bin energy array E_i = |X[k]|^2 indexed by the frequency bins whose centers fall within [f_low, f_high). Computation: the within-band mean mu = (1/N) SUM E_i, then the within-band variance sigma^2 = (1/N) SUM (E_i - mu)^2; the result is a single scalar per frame, typically in normalized relative units or joules squared. It measures how spread out the energy is across the band's bins: a concentrated band (one dominant bin) has low band-variance, an evenly spread band has high. Persistence: recomputed from the input spectrum and the band boundaries at any point in an audio analysis pipeline; it is the second-moment counterpart of spectral-band-centroid (first moment) and the even-order companion to spectral-band-skewness (third) and spectral-band-kurtosis (fourth). Display: {variance, low_hz, high_hz, bins, mean_energy}. [formal: varietas spectralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The onset-envelope is a non-negative real-valued function of time representing the temporal strength of acoustic onsets in an audio signal. Parameters: (1) the input audio signal, (2) the analysis frame rate (samples per second or frames per second), (3) the onset detection function (e.g., spectral flux, energy difference, phase deviation) used to compute raw onset strength, (4) optional smoothing window length for post-processing. Computation: compute the onset detection function frame-by-frame, apply median or exponential smoothing to suppress spurious detections, optionally normalize to [0, 1]. The construct persists as a per-sample or per-frame vector synchronized with the input signal. Display: waveform or scalar trace aligned with audio time. [formal: envelopeum inceptionis | substrate: matter | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The reduction of spectral energy from its peak value across frequency bins. Parameters: (1) discrete power spectrum P[k] for k = 0, ..., N-1 where N is the number of frequency bins, (2) the maximum power value P_max = max_k(P[k]). Persistence mechanism: computed as D[k] = P_max - P[k] for each bin k, yielding a per-bin spectral decrease value; alternatively aggregated as a scalar S = (1/N) * Σ_k(P_max - P[k]) over all bins. Display trailer: spectral-decrease is a scalar or per-bin quantity expressed in the same units as the power spectrum. [formal: diminutio spectralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Spectral-band-crossover is a spectral analysis parameter indicating the frequency within a defined sub-band at which the cumulative energy reaches 50% of the band's total energy — the band-local median frequency. Parameters: (1) the band's lower and upper frequency bounds, (2) the spectral energy values across frequency bins within the band. Computed by sorting frequency bins in ascending order by frequency, accumulating energy until the accumulated total reaches half the band's total energy; the frequency at that point is the crossover point. Distinct from spectral-band-centroid (weighted mean, sensitive to energy outliers) and spectral-band-rolloff (arbitrary threshold like 85%, indicating brightness); the crossover is the energy-median, robust to heavy-tailed distributions. Displayed as a scalar time series over analysis frames. [formal: centrum medium spectrale | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

An analytic signal is a human-made complex-valued signal representation constructed from a real-valued signal x(t) by adding its Hilbert transform H{x(t)} as the imaginary component: z(t) = x(t) + j·H{x(t)}. This construction eliminates all negative-frequency components, resulting in a one-sided spectrum. The analytic signal carries three directly accessible parameters: (1) instantaneous amplitude (envelope) A(t) = |z(t)| = √(x(t)² + H{x(t)}²), (2) instantaneous phase φ(t) = arg(z(t)), and (3) instantaneous frequency f_inst(t) = (1/2π)·dφ/dt. These parameters are computable in real time from a single observation, without ensemble averaging. The construction is used in communications (quadrature modulation/demodulation, SSB generation), audio analysis (phase vocoder phase unwrapping), geophysics, and biomedical signal processing. Persistence mechanism: algorithmic computation standard in DSP libraries (scipy.signal.hilbert, MATLAB hilbert) and embedded in communication system designs. [formal: signalis analyticus | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Spectral peak position is the frequency bin index (or frequency in Hz) of the maximum spectral energy magnitude within a spectrum or subband. Used to identify dominant resonant components. Parameters: search_range (full spectrum or subband), resolution (bin index or frequency). [formal: positio pinnaculi spectralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Instantaneous frequency is a human-made signal processing construct that measures the rate of change of the phase of a signal at each moment in time. It is defined as: f_inst(t) = (1/2π)·dφ(t)/dt, where φ(t) = arg(z(t)) is the instantaneous phase of the analytic signal z(t) = x(t) + j·H{x(t)}, constructed from a real-valued signal x(t) and its Hilbert transform H{x(t)}. Unlike Fourier frequency (which represents a global property of the signal), instantaneous frequency is a local, time-varying quantity that tracks frequency modulation, chirp signals, and time-varying spectral content in real time. Parameters: (1) the phase unwrapping method applied to φ(t) (to avoid discontinuities at ±π), (2) the noise regularization method (to prevent divergence where amplitude is near zero). Persistence mechanism: standard in radar (chirp signal analysis), seismology, speech processing (formant tracking), and biomedical engineering (EEG/ECG frequency modulation analysis), implemented in DSP libraries and embedded in signal analysis instruments. [formal: frequency instantanea | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Stress is the constructed phonological framework for analyzing prominence asymmetry within words and phrases: certain syllables are marked as stressed (more prominent) relative to their neighbors, and this marking is patterned by linguistic rule. Parameters: (1) degree - relative prominence against neighbors, primary and secondary; (2) realization - the cue bundle carrying stress: increased loudness, increased duration, and, in English, pitch height on the stressed syllable; (3) position - placement within the word, rule-governed in many languages and capable of distinguishing word identity (English 'record' noun vs verb); (4) phrase level - the organization of stresses into rhythmic groups in connected speech. Persistence: stress is realized in every utterance, transcribed in phonology, taught in phonetics and language pedagogy, and codified in dictionaries; it persists as a stable parameter of the linguistic system, changing only slowly across generations. [formal: stressum | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The Hilbert transform is a linear operator that shifts the phase of every frequency component of a real-valued signal by 90 degrees (π/2 radians). Mathematically, for a signal x(t), the Hilbert transform is: H{x(t)} = (1/π) PV ∫₋∞^∞ x(τ)/(t−τ) dτ, where PV denotes the Cauchy principal value. In the frequency domain, it acts as an all-pass filter with frequency response H(f) = −j·sgn(f), multiplying positive frequencies by −j and negative frequencies by +j. The transform produces the quadrature component of x(t); combining x(t) with its Hilbert transform yields the analytic signal z(t) = x(t) + j·H{x(t)}, from which instantaneous amplitude (envelope), instantaneous phase, and instantaneous frequency can be derived. Parameters: (1) the input signal domain (continuous-time or discrete via DFT-based implementation), (2) handling of the zero-frequency component (typically set to 0). Persistence mechanism: implemented in DSP libraries (scipy.signal.hilbert, MATLAB hilbert), used in communications (SSB modulation/demodulation), geophysics, and vibration analysis. [formal: transform Hilbert | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Spectral-band-kurtosis is a spectral analysis parameter measuring the fourth standardized moment of spectral energy distribution within a defined frequency sub-band. Parameters: (1) the band's lower and upper frequency bounds, (2) the spectral energy values across frequency bins within the band, (3) the mean and standard deviation of the band's energy distribution. Computed as E[(E - μ)⁴] / σ⁴ where E is spectral energy, μ is the band-mean energy, and σ is the band-standard deviation. High kurtosis indicates a distribution with heavy tails or a sharp peak — energy concentrated in few bins — while low kurtosis indicates a flatter, more uniform energy distribution across the band. Displayed as a scalar time series over analysis frames. [formal: kurtosis spectralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Spectral-band-centroid is a spectral analysis parameter representing the center of mass of spectral energy distribution within a defined frequency sub-band. Parameters: (1) the band's lower and upper frequency bounds, (2) the spectral energy values across frequency bins within the band. Computed as Σ(fᵢ × Eᵢ) / Σ(Eᵢ) where fᵢ is the frequency of bin i and Eᵢ is the spectral energy at that bin — a weighted mean frequency where weights are the per-bin energy values. Indicates whether energy in a band is concentrated toward lower or higher frequencies. Displayed as a scalar time series over analysis frames. [formal: centrum centrotum spectrale | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Spectral-phase-coherence is a measure of how consistently the phase of a frequency component is maintained across a set of analysis frames or segments. Parameters: (1) the frequency band or bin of interest, (2) the frame or segment window over which coherence is measured, (3) the phase values per frame at the target frequency. Computed as the magnitude of the average complex exponential of phase differences across frames, yielding a value in [0,1] where 1 indicates perfect phase consistency and 0 indicates complete phase randomization. The persistence mechanism is the vector averaging of unit phasors derived from phase values at the target frequency. [formal: test | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Accent is the constructed sociolinguistic concept for the phonological component of a speech variety: the distinctive sound patterns by which a listener identifies a speaker's regional or social origin, in the absence of lexical or grammatical difference. Parameters: (1) phonemic inventory - the distinctive vowel and consonant qualities of the accent; (2) articulation - characteristic manner and place of production; (3) prosodic coloring - the intonational and rhythmic quality that colors the accent; (4) indexing - the geographic and social identity the accent signals to listeners. Accent is the phonological part of dialect: dialect is the whole (phonology + lexicon + grammar), and a speaker can be described by the accent alone while sharing the full dialect. Persistence: accent persists in the speech communities that produce it, is transmitted through first-language acquisition and socialization, and is indexed in dialect atlases and sociolinguistic study; it persists as a stable social marker in individual speakers. [formal: accentus | substrate: language | horizon: generations | explicit: no | epoch: 0.4]

Psycholinguistics is a disciplinary framework for mapping the mental representations and processes underlying language production, comprehension, and acquisition. Parameters: processing models, lexical access, syntactic parsing, memory constraints, experimental paradigms, developmental stages. It persists via peer-reviewed experiments, cognitive models, laboratory protocols, and university curricula that replicate findings across populations.

Spectral-octave-band is a frequency subband covering one octave (ratio 2:1 between upper and lower bounds). Parameters: (1) a reference frequency f_ref (typically 1000 Hz), (2) the spectral magnitude or power spectrum P[f] from which subband energy is computed. Definition: the k-th octave band spans [f_ref * 2^(k/2 - 1), f_ref * 2^(k/2 + 1)] for integer k. The subband energy E_k = integral over [f_lo, f_hi] of P[f] df. Persistence: finite set of subband energy values indexed by band number k. [formal: definition | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Corpus-linguistics is a human-made empirical approach to linguistics — the study of language patterns, structures, and usage through systematic analysis of large, representative collections of real-language data (corpora). Two parameters carve the construct: (1) the primary data source is authentic, naturally occurring language recorded in written or spoken form (not introspective or constructed examples), organized into annotated or searchable text collections that sample from defined populations, registers, genres, or time periods; (2) the analytical methods are data-driven and statistical, including frequency analysis, collocation measurement, concordance line examination, n-gram modeling, and distributional semantics, used to discover patterns that may not be predictable from theory alone. Corpus-linguistics persists as a methodological framework that generates empirical descriptions of language (dictionaries, grammars), tests theoretical hypotheses against real usage data, and produces applications in language technology (spell checkers, machine translation, language models), lexicography, and language education. Paradigmatic cases: Brown Corpus frequency analysis, COCA/COHA diachronic corpora, Sketch Engine collocation tools. [formal: corpus-linguistica | substrate: data | horizon: decades | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

Spectral-peak-occupancy is a dimensionless scalar in [0,1] that quantifies the fraction of frequency bins in a power spectrum exceeding a noise-floor threshold. Parameters: (1) a power spectrum P[k] for k = 0, ..., N-1 where N is the number of frequency bins, (2) a noise-floor threshold T expressed as a fraction of the spectral mean (commonly 1-10% of mean power). Persistence mechanism: computed as O = (1/N) * Σ_k I(P[k] > T) where I is the indicator function, yielding a value between 0 (no bins active) and 1 (all bins active). The measure is frame-level, recomputed per analysis window, and persists as a scalar stored alongside other spectral features in audio analysis pipelines. Display: scalar value in [0, 1] expressing the proportion of active spectral bins. [formal: occupatio spectralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]
test [formal: test | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The skewness (third standardized moment) of a power spectrum around its spectral centroid. Parameters: (1) a frequency-binned power or magnitude spectrum S[k] for k=0..K-1, (2) the spectral centroid μ = Σ_k f[k]·S[k] / Σ_k S[k], (3) the spectral bandwidth σ = sqrt(Σ_k (f[k]-μ)²·S[k] / Σ_k S[k]). Computation: skewness = Σ_k (f[k]-μ)³·S[k] / (σ³·Σ_k S[k]). Persistence: the scalar value is stored per spectral frame and recomputed when the spectrum changes. Positive skewness indicates a spectrum with a long tail toward higher frequencies; negative skewness indicates a tail toward lower frequencies.

The chroma filterbank is a fixed 12×N transformation matrix that folds a frequency spectrum into 12 pitch-class bins. Its parameters are: (1) N, the number of frequency bins in the input spectrum (matching the FFT size), (2) the 12 pitch-class center frequencies (typically derived from the equal-tempered scale at 440 Hz reference), and (3) the window function applied to each bin (commonly Gaussian or triangular). The persistence mechanism is the fixed mathematical mapping: for each frame, the filterbank multiplies the spectral vector by the 12×N matrix, summing energy at all frequencies that harmonically correspond to each of the 12 pitch classes (C through B). This produces the octave-invariant chroma vector. The filterbank itself — distinct from the chroma vector it produces — is the transformation kernel, stored as a fixed weight matrix in MIR toolkits (Librosa, Essentia). [formal: chroma-filterbank | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The glottal-source model is a human-made model of the glottal airflow source in speech production, describing the periodic excitation generated by vocal fold vibration. Parameters: fundamental frequency, open quotient, asymmetry coefficient, return phase. Persistence mechanism: the model is formalized as mathematical equations, implemented in speech synthesis software, and taught in speech science; it persists as a reusable component of the source-filter framework. [formal: glottal-source | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.07]

For a frequency band with N energy bins having energies E₁, E₂, ..., Eₙ and total energy E_total = ΣEᵢ, the normalized probability mass function is pᵢ = Eᵢ / E_total. The spectral-band-entropy is H = -Σ pᵢ log₂(pᵢ), where the sum runs over all bins in the band with pᵢ > 0. H measures the uniformity of energy distribution: H = 0 when all energy concentrates in one bin, and H is maximized when energy is uniformly distributed across all bins. [formal: mathematics | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Sociolinguistics is a disciplinary framework for mapping systematic correlations between linguistic variation and social structure. Parameters: speech community, social variables (class, gender, age, ethnicity, region), linguistic variables (phonetic, lexical, syntactic, pragmatic), interactional context and language ideology. It persists via peer-reviewed publications, university curricula, research corpora, and methodological protocols that replicate observations across speech communities.

The angular component of the short-time Fourier transform at each time-frequency bin. Parameters: (1) complex STFT coefficients X[k,t] for frequency bin k and time frame t, (2) frequency resolution bin spacing Δf = fs/(2N) where fs is the sampling rate and N is the window size. Persistence mechanism: computed as φ[k,t] = arg(X[k,t]) via the atan2 function yielding φ[k,t] ∈ (-π, π] radians; the phase encodes the relative timing of sinusoidal components within each analysis window. Display trailer: spectral-phase is a real-valued function of discrete frequency and time, expressed in radians or cycles. [formal: phase spectralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The root-mean-square energy of a discrete signal over a window of N samples. Parameters: (1) the signal samples x[n] for n in the analysis window, (2) the window length N. Computation: square each sample, compute the arithmetic mean of the squared values, take the square root. Persistence: the scalar value is stored per window and recomputed when samples or window bounds change. This operates directly on time-domain samples, not on any spectral representation.

Spectral-band-flux is a temporal descriptor measuring the frame-to-frame rate of change of spectral energy within a defined frequency band. Parameters: (1) the band lower and upper frequency bounds, (2) the current and preceding analysis frames, (3) the spectral-band-energy values at each frame. Computed as the absolute difference of spectral-band-energy between consecutive frames, yielding a non-negative value representing the magnitude of energy change regardless of direction. The persistence mechanism is the subtraction of accumulated band energy values across time-ordered frame pairs. [formal: test | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The onset-strength is a non-negative real-valued function of time representing the intensity of acoustic onsets per analysis frame. Parameters: (1) the input audio signal, (2) the analysis frame rate. The persistence mechanism computes a per-frame onset strength value, typically via spectral flux |P(f,t)−P(f,t−1)| or energy-based methods, yielding a non-negative scalar per frame that quantifies how strongly an onset is present. [formal: onset-strength | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

Tempo-estimation infers the beat rate of a periodic audio signal in beats per minute (BPM). Parameters: (1) the input audio signal or its envelope/attack-decay representation, (2) the analysis window duration over which tempo is estimated, (3) the BPM search range [min_bpm, max_bpm] typically [30, 300]. Computation: extract an onset/energy envelope, compute an autocorrelation or beat-spectrum over candidate BPM lags, select the peak within the search range as the estimated tempo. The construct persists as a single scalar BPM value per analyzed segment. Display: scalar in beats per minute, typically rounded to the nearest integer. [formal: estimatio temporis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Spectral-tile is a two-dimensional matrix T[t,f] where each cell (t,f) stores the magnitude or power value of a signal spectrum at time frame t and frequency bin f. Parameters: (1) a sequence of spectral frames S[f,t] from an STFT or filterbank, (2) a normalization function N applied per-frame or globally. The matrix is persisted as a 2D array with time on one axis and frequency on the other, enabling visualization as a heat map and computation via 2D convolution. Display: T[t,f] = N(S[f,t]) [formal: mind | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Accent is the sociolinguistic category that isolates the phonological component of a speech variety as an independently indexable unit: the sound patterns by which a listener identifies a speaker's regional or social origin, abstracted from lexical and grammatical difference. Parameters: (1) isolation rule — the map draws its boundary by holding lexicon and grammar constant and varying only the phonological system (the 'same words, different sound' test); (2) indexed content — the origin the category encodes: regional (e.g., Scots, Geordie, Australian) or social (e.g., RP, AAVE); (3) descriptive levels the map organizes — phonemic inventory, articulation, prosodic coloring; (4) contrast frame — an accent is defined against a reference variety within the same language. Persistence: the category is maintained as an instrument of the discipline — dialect atlases (Survey of English Dialects), sociolinguistic textbooks and curricula, accent-labeling practice in media and pedagogy, and listening-identification tests — drawn, taught, and revised by sociolinguists; it is maintained by the discipline, not transmitted by speakers. [formal: accentus | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A chromagram is a time-frequency representation that maps spectral energy into mel-warped frequency bins per analysis frame. It is computed by applying a mel-scale filterbank to spectral energy and summing energy within each mel band. [formal: chromagramma | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Spectral-band-flatness is a spectral analysis parameter measuring how uniform the energy distribution is within a defined frequency sub-band. Parameters: (1) the band's lower and upper frequency bounds, (2) the spectral energy values across frequency bins within the band. Computed as the ratio of the geometric mean to the arithmetic mean of the band's per-bin energy values: (Π Eᵢ)^(1/N) / (Σ Eᵢ / N), where Eᵢ is the energy at bin i and N is the number of bins. Values range from 0 (highly non-uniform, energy concentrated in few bins) to 1 (perfectly uniform energy distribution across all bins in the band). Displayed as a scalar time series over analysis frames. [formal: planities spectralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A filterbank is a bank of interrelated bandpass filters that decomposes an input signal into multiple frequency sub-bands. Parameters: (1) number of filters — the count of distinct sub-bands; (2) center frequencies — the passband center for each filter; (3) bandwidth — the width of each passband (often constant-Q or constant-percent-bandwidth); (4) overlap factor — whether sub-bands overlap in frequency. The filterbank operates by routing the input signal through each bandpass filter, producing a set of sub-band outputs where each represents the signal energy within a specific frequency range. The persistence mechanism is algorithmic computation: the filterbank is implemented as a cascade or parallel array of filter coefficients in DSP software libraries (librosa, kaldi, MATLAB) and hardware DSP pipelines, applied to signals as a deterministic transformation. [formal: banca filtri | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A cepstrum is the power spectrum of the log-power spectrum of a signal. Computed by: taking the Fourier transform of the signal, computing the log of the magnitude spectrum, then computing the inverse Fourier transform of the log-magnitude spectrum. Parameters: window size for the initial transform, overlap for overlap-add reconstruction. The cepstrum separates periodic structures in the spectrum (such as formant echoes in speech or pitch harmonics) into distinct peaks at quefrency positions corresponding to the delay between reflections. Persistence mechanism: the cepstrum is computed as a deterministic mathematical transform, implemented in speech analysis and audio processing software, and used as an intermediate representation in cepstral feature extraction pipelines. [formal: cepstrum | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

spectral-band-moment is a family of numerical descriptors derived from the distribution of spectral energy within a defined frequency band. Parameters: (1) band lower and upper frequency bounds, (2) the order r of the moment, (3) the per-bin spectral energy values within the band, (4) analysis frame window. Computed as the r-th central moment of the energy distribution, normalized where appropriate, yielding a scalar per frame. Persistence mechanism: standardized mathematical definitions used in signal processing and audio analysis. [formal: momentum spectralis | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.60]

spectral-band-slope(f_low, f_high) = slope of linear regression of log10(E[i]) against f_center[i], for all bins i where f_low <= f_center[i] < f_high, expressed in dB/Hz. Parameters: f_low (Hz, lower band boundary), f_high (Hz, upper band boundary), sampling_rate (Hz), n_fft (int, FFT window size). Persistence: least-squares slope fit over the log-energy vs. frequency points within the band. Distinguishes spectral-band-centroid (mean-weighted center of mass) from spectral-band-slope (direction and magnitude of energy tilt). [formal: spectral-band-slope | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

A crest-factor is a human-made audio engineering metric that quantifies the ratio of peak amplitude to RMS amplitude of a signal. Parameters: (1) A_peak = max|A(t)| the peak amplitude, (2) A_rms = √(1/T ∫₀ᵀ A(t)² dt) the RMS amplitude over window T. The persistence mechanism is the scalar ratio: CF = A_peak / A_rms. Used to characterize the dynamic profile of audio signals, distinguish percussive from sustained sounds. |crest-factor| CF = A_peak / A_rms |2025-01-01| Ezra

An utterance is the human-constructed concept for a contiguous stretch of speech or writing that participants in a communicative event treat as a single, bounded unit of action. Parameters: (1) physical extent — the actual span of vocal articulation or written symbols, from first sound/symbol to last; (2) communicative boundary — the participants' shared understanding of where this unit begins and ends, which may diverge from grammatical boundaries (an utterance may span multiple sentences or be a fragment of one); (3) functional unit — the utterance performs some recoverable communicative function within the ongoing interaction. Distinction from related constructs: a sentence is a grammatical unit defined by syntactic rules; a speech act is the action performed by an utterance (one utterance may realize multiple speech acts); discourse is the larger organized structure of multiple utterances. Persistence: maintained through transcription conventions, dialogue annotation frameworks, and the analytical practices of pragmatics and discourse analysis. [formal: uterantia | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Spectral-variance quantifies the dispersion of power values across frequency bins. Given a power spectrum P[k] for k = 0..N-1, the spectral mean μ = (1/N)ΣP[k] and the spectral variance σ² = (1/N)Σ(P[k] - μ)². Parameters: (1) the power spectrum P[k] as the input domain, (2) the normalization scheme (mean or total-power normalization). The persistence mechanism is the second central moment of P[k] over the frequency index, which distinguishes narrowband spectra (low variance) from broadband spectra (high variance). [formal: spectralis varietas | substrate: matter | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Spectral peak rolloff is a parameter identifying the frequency below which a specified percentage (typically 85%) of the total spectral energy accumulates. It serves as a robust measure of spectral centroid, less sensitive to outliers than the spectral centroid. Parameters: rolloff_percent (default 0.85, range 0-1). Computed by sorting spectral magnitudes in descending order, accumulating their squared values, and finding the frequency at which the cumulative sum reaches rolloff_percent times the total spectral energy. [formal: spectral-peak-rolloff | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

For a frequency band with N energy bins having energies E_1, E_2, ..., E_N within frequencies f_1, f_2, ..., f_N: the effective bandwidth is the ratio of the sum of energies to the maximum energy, scaled by the per-bin frequency spacing delta_f. The parameter is the frequency band definition (lower and upper bounds). The persistence mechanism is BW = (sum(E_i) / max(E_i)) * delta_f where delta_f = (f_upper - f_lower) / N. Display trailer: [formal: effective bandwidth | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Spectral tenuity is a metric quantifying how thin or filamentary the spectral energy distribution is across frequency bins. Unlike sparseness which measures concentration count, tenuity measures the ratio of peak energy to total energy, capturing how narrowly energy clusters around dominant components. Computed as peak magnitude divided by mean magnitude across active bins. [formal: tenuitas spectralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Spectral-roll-off is a frequency value in Hz that marks the point below which a specified cumulative fraction (default 0.85) of the total spectral energy is contained. Parameters: (1) a power spectrum P[k] for k = 0, ..., N-1 with associated frequency bins f[k], (2) a cumulative threshold τ ∈ [0,1] (default 0.85). Computation: sort P[k] by f[k], compute cumulative sum C[k] = Σ_{i=0}^{k} P[i], then find the smallest k* such that C[k*]/Σ_{i=0}^{N-1} P[i] ≥ τ; roll-off = f[k*]. Display: roll-off(τ) = f[k*] where C[k*]/E_total ≥ τ and C[k*-1]/E_total < τ [formal: mind | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The time required for an amplitude envelope to fall from its peak level to a specified lower level after the attack phase. Parameters: (1) initial amplitude A_peak at onset, (2) target amplitude A_target (commonly −60 dB relative to peak), (3) reference times t_peak and t_target marking when the envelope reaches each level. Persistence mechanism: computed as τ_decay = t_target − t_peak, where t_target is the earliest time after t_peak such that the envelope amplitude A(t) ≤ A_target for all t ∈ [t_target, t_end]. Display trailer: decay-time is a scalar duration expressed in seconds, milliseconds, or samples. [formal: tempus decadentiae | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Spectral-flow is the temporal evolution of spectral energy distribution across consecutive analysis frames, capturing how energy moves between frequency bands over time. Parameters: (1) spectral resolution — bin width in Hz or mel-scale, (2) temporal resolution — frame rate in Hz, (3) aggregation function — L1 norm, L2 norm, or KL-divergence for measuring inter-frame change. The persistence mechanism maps (spectrum sequence, aggregation) to a continuous trajectory function f(t) describing spectral centroid position, bandwidth, and flux over time. [formal: spectralis fluxus | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The spectral-difference is a non-negative real-valued vector of per-frequency-bin absolute differences between consecutive power spectra. Parameters: (1) the power spectrum at time frame t, (2) the power spectrum at time frame t−1. The persistence mechanism computes |P(f,t) − P(f,t−1)| for each frequency bin f, yielding a vector quantifying spectral change between adjacent frames. [formal: spectral-difference | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

spectral-band-mode is a CONCEPT filing for a spectral analysis parameter that identifies the mode of the spectral energy distribution within a defined frequency sub-band. Parameters: (1) lower and upper frequency bounds of the sub-band, (2) the spectral resolution of the underlying FFT or transform, (3) the bin-count within the sub-band. Persistence mechanism: the frequency bin with the highest spectral energy amplitude within the defined sub-band, computed as argmax of the band-limited energy histogram. The mode indicates the dominant spectral component within a narrow sub-band, complementing the centroid (mean) and variance (spread) descriptors. [formal: spectral-band-mode | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Spectral sparseness is a metric quantifying how concentrated spectral energy is across frequency bins. High sparseness indicates energy concentrated in few bins (e.g. tonal signals); low sparseness indicates diffuse energy (e.g. noise). Computed as (sum of magnitudes)^2 divided by (number_of_bins times sum of squared magnitudes). [formal: sparsitas spectralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A bark-spectrogram is a two-dimensional time-frequency matrix where rows are bark-scale frequency bins and columns are temporal frames. Parameters: (1) N bark-scale bins indexed 0..N-1, (2) frame hop size h in samples, (3) window function w applied per frame. Computation: for each frame f, apply FFT to windowed segment, convert linear-frequency indices to bark scale via Bark(f) = 13*arctan(0.00076*f) + 3.5*arctan((f/7500)^2), accumulate energy into bark bins, normalize by bin bandwidth. Persistence: the matrix values are the squared magnitudes accumulated per bark bin, stored as a sequence of N×T matrices. Display: a heatmap with time on the x-axis, Bark units on the y-axis, color representing log-energy.

Lexeme is a human-made conceptual category — the minimal meaningful unit of a language that functions as the basic item in the mental lexicon of speakers. Three parameters carve the construct: (1) minimal meaningfulness: the lexeme carries semantic content that cannot be decomposed into smaller meaningful parts within that language's grammar, distinguishing it from phrases or complex words whose meaning is compositional; (2) identity-independence: the lexeme has a single abstract identity across all its surface forms — inflectional variants (walk/walks/walked/walking) and allomorphic variants (happy/happiness) express the same lexeme, while a shift in core meaning or derivational structure marks a different lexeme; (3) mental reality: lexemes are stored and retrieved by speakers as discrete units in the mental lexicon, not as lists of word forms. Lexemes persist as the atomic referent of grammatical description, lexical semantics, and word-formation rules. [formal: lexema | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

For a frequency band with N energy bins having energies E_1, E_2, ..., E_N: the crest factor CF = max(E_i) / RMS, where RMS = sqrt((1/N) * sum(E_i^2)). The parameter is the frequency band definition (lower and upper bounds). The persistence mechanism is the dimensionless ratio CF = max(E_i) * sqrt(N) / sqrt(sum(E_i^2)). Display trailer: [formal: crest factor | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Spectral-crest is a dimensionless ratio expressing the concentration of spectral energy at the peak bin relative to the mean across all bins. Parameters: (1) a power spectrum P[k] or magnitude spectrum |X[k]| for k = 0, ..., N-1. When using power spectrum: crest = max(P[k]) / (1/N Σ P[k]). When using magnitude: crest = max(|X[k]|) / (1/N Σ |X[k]|). The ratio is expressed in dB: crest_dB = 10·log₁₀(crest). Display: crest = max_k(P[k]) / mean_k(P[k]) [formal: mind | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Spectral-band-rolloff is a spectral analysis parameter indicating the frequency below which a specified percentage (typically 85%) of the total spectral energy within a defined frequency sub-band is concentrated. Parameters: (1) the band's lower and upper frequency bounds, (2) the spectral energy values across frequency bins within the band, (3) the energy threshold percentage (default 85%). Computed by sorting frequency bins in ascending order by frequency and accumulating energy until the accumulated energy reaches the threshold fraction of the band's total energy; the frequency at that point is the rolloff point. Indicates the spectral 'brightness' or high-frequency content within a band. Displayed as a scalar time series over analysis frames. [formal: reiectura spectralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Computational linguistics is a disciplinary framework for formalizing linguistic knowledge in algorithms and computational models. Parameters: corpus design, statistical models, symbolic grammars, evaluation metrics, processing pipelines. It persists via open-source software, benchmark datasets, peer-reviewed publications, and university curricula that replicate model performance across tasks.

The ratio of the maximum magnitude bin in a spectrum to the root-mean-square magnitude across all bins. Parameters: (1) discrete magnitude spectrum |X[k]| for k = 0, …, N−1, where N is the number of frequency bins, (2) the index k_max at which |X[k]| is maximized. Persistence mechanism: computed as C_spectral = |X[k_max]| / sqrt((1/N) * Σ|X[k]|²), where the sum spans all bins. The ratio is a dimensionless scalar. Display trailer: spectral-crest-factor is a dimensionless quantity, typically expressed in decibels as 20·log₁₀(C_spectral). [formal: cresta spectralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The spectral kurtosis is the kurtosis (fourth standardized moment) of the spectral power distribution across frequency bins. Parameters: (1) the power-spectrum over which kurtosis is computed, (2) the normalization reference (typically the mean power squared). Computation: kurtosis = E[(P - μ)^4] / E[(P - μ)^2]^2 where P is the power spectrum and μ is its mean. The measure detects impulsive or non-stationary components in a signal by identifying frequency bins with heavy-tailed power distributions. The construct persists as a single scalar value per analyzed segment. Display: scalar, typically expressed in decibels. [formal: kurtosis spectralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A processing technique in which a signal's amplitude envelope is extracted and used to modulate or track another signal. Parameters: (1) input signal x(t), (2) envelope extraction stage (rectification followed by low-pass filtering with time constant τ, or Hilbert transform followed by magnitude extraction), (3) output modulation rate governed by attack time τ_a and decay/release time τ_r. Persistence mechanism: the envelope e(t) is computed as e(t) = LP{x(t) · h_LP(t)} where h_LP is a low-pass filter impulse response characterized by τ_a for upward transitions and τ_r for downward transitions; this envelope then drives a gain stage, frequency shifter, or other parameterized element. Display trailer: envelope-following is a behavioral pattern instantiated in specific circuits or algorithms such as auto-wah, tremolo, or sidechain compression. [formal: sequentia involucri | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Delta coefficients are first-order time derivatives of cepstral coefficients, capturing the temporal trajectory of the spectral envelope. Computed by fitting a least-squares linear regression over a window of cepstral coefficient frames. Used in speech recognition to model temporal dynamics beyond static spectral shape. [formal: coefficients delta | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Linguistic register is the map of the system of situationally differentiated language varieties a speech community develops and maintains — the varieties a community deploys for different communicative situations (colloquial, formal, technical, ceremonial, professional) — carved along three parameters. (1) The situational axis: the dimensions along which the varieties are organized are field (the subject matter and activity in which the language is deployed), tenor (the social relations and roles between participants), and mode (the channel and the participatory structure of the discourse); a variety is a conventionalized set of lexical, grammatical, and prosodic choices indexed to the situation, so that the same speaker deploys different varieties in different situations. (2) The boundary lines that separate the map from its neighbours: register is indexed to situation, which distinguishes it from dialect (indexed to region and social group) and from genre (a type of discourse text rather than a variety of the language itself); and it is distinct from the institutional register — an official list maintained by an authority with legal or institutional force — in that a linguistic register is updated by the speech community's convention, not by institutional mandate, and no authority stands behind its entries. (3) The map, not the territory: the entry names the systematic description the community and the discipline build over the natural variation of speech — the inventory of varieties and the dimensions that organize it — not the natural variation itself. Persistence: the varieties persist as social convention — acquired in socialization, maintained through institutional reinforcement (courts, academies, professions, liturgy), and relearned by each generation; the map persists as the stable sub-field of linguistics called register analysis, its dimensions codified in textbooks and corpora. [formal: regiter linguae | substrate: behavior | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.05]

Neurolinguistics is a human-made interdisciplinary field — the study of the neural and biological mechanisms that underlie language acquisition, processing, representation, and comprehension. Two parameters carve the construct: (1) the explanatory level is biological/neural (brain anatomy, neural circuits, electrophysiological responses, neuroimaging data, lesion studies, and molecular markers), not purely behavioral or computational; (2) the phenomenon explained is language in its full range — phonology, syntax, semantics, pragmatics, lexicon, acquisition, and breakdown — treated as operations implemented by neural systems. Neurolinguistics persists as an active research enterprise that generates testable hypotheses about how the brain implements language, uses these hypotheses to interpret clinical conditions (aphasia, dyslexia, speech disorders), and informs brain-computer interfaces for language restoration. Paradigmatic methods: fMRI and EEG mapping of language tasks, lesion-symptom mapping in aphasia patients, intracranial electrophysiology, and computational modeling of neural language processing. [formal: neurolinguistica | substrate: brain | horizon: decades | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

Intonation is the constructed linguistic framework for analyzing pitch-contour organization in spoken language: the way fundamental frequency rises and falls across the duration of an utterance, and the way those movements are patterned by linguistic rule rather than speaker whim. Parameters: (1) pitch contour - the F0 trajectory across the utterance, rising, falling, or level; (2) tone unit - the stretch of speech over which a single contour operates, delimited by pauses; (3) nuclear stress - the syllable carrying the principal tone of the tone unit; (4) grammatical and attitudinal function - contour used to mark clause type (interrogative vs declarative), focus, and attitude (e.g., English rising terminals for yes-no questions). Persistence: intonation is realized in every produced utterance, analyzed in intonation notation (e.g., ToBI), taught in language pedagogy, and studied in phonology; it persists as long as speech carries meaning through pitch. [formal: intonatio | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The crest factor of a signal is the ratio of its peak amplitude to its root-mean-square value. Parameters: (1) the signal samples x[n] over an analysis window, (2) the peak amplitude max|x[n]|, (3) the RMS value computed over the same window. Computation: crest = max|x[n]| / RMS(x[n]). Display: [DSP: descriptor, units: dimensionless]

Historical linguistics is a disciplinary framework for reconstructing diachronic change in language systems from attested corpora. Parameters: comparative method, sound change laws, attestation dates, textual corpora, reconstruction techniques. It persists via published reconstructions, philological editions, comparative datasets, and university curricula that transmit methodological standards across generations.

The source-filter model is a human-made mathematical model of speech production that decomposes the speech signal generation into a source component, typically the glottal airflow with fundamental frequency, and a filter component, the vocal tract transfer function shaping formants. Parameters: source excitation model, filter order, formant frequencies and bandwidths, glottal pulse shape. Persistence mechanism: the model is formalized in equations, implemented in speech synthesis and analysis software, and taught in speech science curricula; it persists as a reusable theoretical framework. [formal: source-filter-model | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.07]

Spectral-band-energy is a spectral analysis parameter representing the total energy accumulated within a defined frequency sub-band of a spectrum at a given analysis frame. Parameters: (1) the band's lower and upper frequency bounds (e.g., ISO 266 third-octave band edges or arbitrary analyst-specified limits), (2) the spectral resolution (frequency bin width) of the underlying transform. Computed as the sum of squared magnitude values |X[k]|² across all frequency bins k whose center frequencies fall within [f_low, f_high). The result is a scalar energy value per frame, typically expressed in joules or a normalized relative scale. Persists as a time series of per-frame scalar values in audio analysis pipelines, used as input to higher-order parameters like spectral-band-flux, spectral-band-skewness, and other band-localized descriptors. [formal: spectral-band-energy | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The spectral kurtosis is the kurtosis (fourth standardized moment) of the spectral power distribution computed across frequency bins. Parameters: (1) the power spectrum S[k] for k=0..K-1, (2) the spectral centroid μ = Σ_k f[k]·S[k] / Σ_k S[k]. Computation: κ = Σ_k (f[k]-μ)⁴·S[k] / (σ⁴·Σ_k S[k]) where σ is the spectral standard deviation. Display: [DSP: descriptor, units: dimensionless]

A sociolect is a variety of language associated with a particular social group or social class, distinguished by systematic conventions in lexicon, pronunciation, and grammar that mark group membership. It operates through shared linguistic practices that emerge from common social experiences, institutional affiliations, or cultural positions — distinct from dialects (which are geographic) and registers (which are situational). Parameters include the social boundary that defines the group (occupation, education level, socioeconomic status, subculture), the degree of linguistic convergence or divergence from the broader vernacular, and the social indexicality of distinctive forms. Persistence mechanism: sociolects persist as living practice within groups — reproduced through social interaction, reinforced through identity marking, and maintained through the group's internal need for linguistic solidarity, independent of any formal codification or institutional support. [formal: sociolectus | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.50]

Pitch class distribution is a histogram representing the energy distribution across the 12 pitch classes (C, C#, D, D#, E, F, F#, G, G#, A, A#, B) of the chromatic scale, independent of octave. Computed by summing spectral energy into the 12 pitch classes via pitch-class transform. Used in MIR for chord detection and tonal analysis. [formal: distributio classum harmonicarum | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Cognitive-linguistics is a human-made approach to linguistics — the study of language as a manifestation of general cognitive abilities, including categorization, conceptualization, metaphorical reasoning, and embodied experience. Two parameters carve the construct: (1) the explanatory framework denies that language operates as an autonomous module separate from general cognition; language structure reflects domain-general cognitive mechanisms like attention, memory, pattern recognition, and conceptual blending; (2) the empirical evidence comes from cross-linguistic analysis of how semantic structure, syntactic patterns, and figurative language systematically reflect cognitive universals (spatial reasoning, embodiment, force-dynamics) rather than language-internal formal rules. Cognitive-linguistics persists as a theoretical framework that produces models of construction grammar, conceptual metaphor theory, and cognitive semantics, generating testable predictions about language use, acquisition, and processing that compete with modularist accounts. Paradigmatic cases: conceptual metaphor analysis (e.g., ARGUMENT IS WAR), construction grammar descriptions, image-schema theory. [formal: cognitio-linguistica | substrate: mind | horizon: decades | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Spectral-band-skewness is a statistical descriptor of how the distribution of spectral energy within a defined frequency band deviates from symmetry. Parameters: (1) the band lower and upper frequency bounds, (2) the analysis frame or frame window, (3) the energy values per frequency bin within the band. Computed as the normalized third central moment of the energy distribution across bins within the band, yielding a dimensionless value where positive values indicate right-skewed distributions toward higher frequencies and negative values indicate left-skewed distributions. The persistence mechanism is the arithmetic computation over the finite set of bin energy values for the given band and frame. [formal: test | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

An instantaneous-amplitude is a human-made signal processing construct that extracts the time-varying envelope of an analytic signal as its complex magnitude. Parameters: (1) z(t) = x(t) + j·H{x(t)} the analytic signal, (2) φ(t) = arg(z(t)) the instantaneous phase. The persistence mechanism is pointwise magnitude: A(t) = |z(t)| = √(x(t)² + H{x(t)}²). Used for amplitude demodulation and envelope analysis in communication systems. |instantaneous-amplitude| A(t) = |z(t)| = √(x(t)² + H{x(t)}²) |2025-01-01| Ezra

Spectral-band-mode is a spectral analysis parameter identifying the most frequently occurring energy value among spectral bins within a defined frequency sub-band. Parameters: (1) the frequency sub-band boundaries (low, high in Hz), (2) the per-bin energy array E_i indexed by frequency bin i. The mode is computed by constructing a histogram of per-bin energy values within the band and returning the bin of the histogram with maximum count; ties are broken by selecting the lowest energy value. Persistence: recomputed from the input spectrum and the band boundaries at any point. Display: {mode_hz, low_hz, high_hz, bins}. [formal: math | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Derivation is a human-made morphological operation — the process by which a language creates a new lexeme from an existing one by adding derivational material. Three parameters carve the construct: (1) lexeme change: the output is a new lexeme with a distinct dictionary identity from the input (happy → happiness is one lexeme becoming another; walk → walked is NOT derivation, because walked is an inflected form of the same lexeme as walk). This lexeme-change criterion is the decisive boundary from inflection. (2) derivational material: the operation is carried by a bound morpheme (affix) or, in some languages, by a change of stress, vowel, or other internal modification that contributes derivational meaning (English sing → song: an ablaut-derived noun; by contrast the tense forms sang and sung remain inflected forms of the same lexeme as sing). (3) conventionalized meaning: the derivational material contributes a systematic, predictable meaning (-ness 'state of being', un- 'negation', -er 'agent') that transforms the input lexeme's meaning in a rule-governed way. Paradigmatic cases: happy + -ness → happiness (new lexeme); write → writer (new lexeme, agentive). Derivation persists as a productive rule — speakers coin new derived lexemes on the fly — and as a stable category of grammatical description: derivational affixes are catalogued in the morphological inventory of each language. [formal: derivatio | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]
